immutable.why: Strings are immutable: toUpperCase returns a new String and leaves s unchanged. The first call's result is thrown away; the second is assigned back to s.

slicing.why: substring(2, 5) takes indices 2, 3 and 4 (the end index is exclusive): t, e, r. indexOf returns the first match, at index 3. The last character is at length() - 1.

split-empty.why: split keeps empty strings between separators (the one between the two commas) and only drops trailing empty strings.

equals-vs-identity.why: That's exactly the difference. Two Strings built separately can have equal characters but be different objects, so always compare String contents with equals.

concat-loop.why: Each += creates a new String and copies everything built so far: 1 + 2 + … + n characters in total, which is quadratic. StringBuilder appends in amortized constant time, making the loop O(n).

reverse.why: StringBuilder.reverse() reverses the builder's characters in place and returns the builder, so toString() gives the reversed text.

builder-why.why: Every += allocates a new String and copies the old contents. StringBuilder keeps one buffer that grows occasionally. (It's StringBuffer that's synchronized, and nobody needs that here.)
